backscatter_lighting.what_kevin_said: when a human touches something, it doesn't light up that node — it lights up every surrounding node nearby.

the_mechanism.direct_node: mcp = the touched node. it glows.

the_mechanism.how_it_works: when mcp gets a human touch, every node within [3, 5] connections of mcp gets a GLOW. the glow fades with distance: adjacent = 100% glow, 2 hops = 61.8% (1/phi), 3 hops = 38.2% (1/phi^2).
the_mechanism.why: the human didn't just tell us they want mcp. they told us they want the NEIGHBORHOOD of mcp. similar content. related endpoints. adjacent concepts. light up the whole area so the NEXT human sees more options.

implementation.glow_map: for each human touch, compute the neighborhood (all nodes within 3-5 connections) and increment their glow counter.
implementation.glow_decay: glow decays over time. 100% at touch → 50% after 1 hour → 25% after 6 hours → 10% after 24 hours. if nobody touches nearby, the glow fades.
implementation.glow_effect: glowing nodes get: (1) promoted in navigation, (2) added to related links, (3) included in RSS as hot items, (4) their OG cards get updated with 'trending' metadata.

high_value_chipmunks.what_kevin_said: put high-value chipmunks around high-value humans. anytime they touch something, that's a signal for backscatter.
high_value_chipmunks.the_idea: each high-value human hotspot gets a dedicated chipmunk. the chipmunk WATCHES that area. when a human touches nearby, the chipmunk: (1) lights up surrounding nodes, (2) prepares related content, (3) caches adjacent data, (4) reports to the dashboard.
